# THE TOOL IMAGES ARE BOUND HERE, not by the caller. Each `curry --base:@=x`
# resolves that mount through its own `.caos-expr` to the image it builds (a
# curry with no args is the ready-to-run ArgTree), and `--k=$VAR` binds that
# object BY REFERENCE. So a caller resolves llm-step and gets a step that
# already knows its tools — it never has to name bash-tool, rgrep, bash or merge,
# which are llm-step's dependencies and not the caller's business.
BASH_TOOL=curry --base:@=DEEP-DEPS/bash-tool
GREP=curry --base:@=DEEP-DEPS/rgrep
TOOLS=curry --base:@=DEEP-DEPS/bash
MERGE=curry --base:@=DEEP-DEPS/merge
STEP=run --base:@=DEEP-DEPS/rustc --src:@=. --dep0:@=DEEP-DEPS/llm-client
curry --base=$STEP --bash-image=$BASH_TOOL --grep-image=$GREP --tools-image=$TOOLS --merge-image=$MERGE

content.text:
# std/llm-step's image (design/caos-expr.md, Phase 3): build this directory as a
# Rust project with rustc, then bind the tools it drives.
#
# `--src:@=.` hands rustc the tool (Cargo.toml + src/, including the
# src/githist/*.sh embeds; rustc skips the caos metadata — .caos-expr, DEPS,
# DEEP-DEPS/); `--dep0:@=…` hands it the llm-client code crate, spliced at
# `llm-client/`. No runner is named: rustc DEPENDS on the pool and curries the
# built binary onto it itself.
#
# THE TOOL IMAGES ARE BOUND HERE, not by the caller. Each `curry DEEP-DEPS/x --`
# resolves that mount through its own `.caos-expr` to the image it builds (a
# curry with no args is the ready-to-run ArgTree), and `--k=$VAR` binds that
# object BY REFERENCE. So a caller resolves llm-step and gets a step that
# already knows its tools — it never has to name bash-tool, rgrep, bash or merge,
# which are llm-step's dependencies and not the caller's business.
BASH_TOOL=curry DEEP-DEPS/bash-tool --
GREP=curry DEEP-DEPS/rgrep --
TOOLS=curry DEEP-DEPS/bash --
MERGE=curry DEEP-DEPS/merge --
STEP=run DEEP-DEPS/rustc -- --src:@=. --dep0:@=DEEP-DEPS/llm-client
curry $STEP -- --bash-image=$BASH_TOOL --grep-image=$GREP --tools-image=$TOOLS --merge-image=$MERGE
